description: The donut chart illustrates the distribution of topics within the $M^3EL$ dataset, which is designed for multi-modal entity linking. It is divided into five distinct categories, each represented by a colored segment with its corresponding percentage: “Common” (light blue, 41.2%), “Person” (light pink, 30.5%), “Book” (light yellow, 9.1%), “Sport” (light purple, 4.3%), and an unlabeled category (light green, 14.9%) that appears in the legend as “Common” but is visually distinct from the 41.2% segment — suggesting a possible labeling inconsistency or an additional subcategory. The chart includes a central legend titled “Topics” that maps each color to its label, and percentage values are displayed directly on the outer ring of the donut. The segments are arranged in descending order of size clockwise from the top, with the largest segment (“Common” at 41.2%) occupying nearly half the chart, followed by “Person,” then the unlabeled green segment, “Book,” and finally “Sport,” which is the smallest. The visual design emphasizes the dominance of “Common” and “Person” topics in the dataset.
